<cite ref="Mishnah Mikvaot 10:1">Mikv. X, 1</cite> <he>ק׳ הדיוטות וכ׳</he> (read: <he>הדיוטית</he> or <he>של הדיוטות</he>) the inkstand of ordinary men (with a rim bent inside to prevent spilling) does not become clean by immersion until you make a hole in its side; <he>וק׳ של יוסף הכהן וכ׳</he> and the inkstand of Joseph the priest (Josephus Flavius?) had a hole in its side (through which it could be emptied and cleaned).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 3:1:21">Y. Ab. Zar. III, 42ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>הנייר … ק׳ צריכה</he> paper and pen are considered ornamental objects (with regard to idolatrous decorations on them); as to the inkstand, it is doubtful.

<cite ref="Shabbat 80a">Sabb. 80ᵃ</cite> <he>בק׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>בקומרין</he>, ed. Sonc. <he>בקלרין</he>, corr. acc.) forming a letter by dropping ink out of the inkstand.—Pl. <cite ref="S01365"><he>קַלְמָרִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="S01366"><he>קַלְמָרִין</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 2:7">Kel. II, 7</cite> <he>ק׳ המותאמות</he> ed. Dehr. (oth. ed. <he>המתואמות</he>; Ar. <he>המתאמת</he> sing.) a double inkstand (v. Sm. Ant. s. v. Atramentum).
